author: reek
body: A runnable model of a real-time ocean surface. This is the simulation the water shader would evaluate on the GPU, expressed as a program that samples the surface at discrete points and reports displacement, normal, foam, and shaded colour. A point goes in, a lit sample comes out.

author: reek
body: A flat 3-vector reused for positions, normals, and colours.

author: reek
body: The accumulator gathers, across all waves at one point: the three displacement components, the surface gradient used to build the normal, and the three Jacobian terms of the horizontal displacement (the fold measure that tells us where crests pinch and throw foam).

author: reek
body: A sampled surface point: the displaced world position, the unit normal, the Jacobian, and the foam coverage derived from it.

author: reek
body: Subsurface scattering: light that enters a wave crest and scatters toward the eye. Strongest when the view looks back along a normal-distorted light direction, i.e. through a lit crest toward the sun. Purely view-and-light driven, no volume integration.

author: reek
body: This chapter is a library and carries no entry point. It had one, back when it was the only file here: a driver that sampled four points and printed them. A chapter with an `opening` cannot be cited by a program that has its own, so keeping it here would have meant every reader of the model duplicating it instead.

author: reek
body: The four-sample driver is `OceanSamples`, unchanged in what it prints. `OceanRender` draws the same model as an image.
